analyses.reason: Same as `crises`. `analyse` is a real verb, so this picks the pair a player means and lets `analyse`/`analyses` through. The technical siblings (`dialyses`, `hydrolyses`, `fibroses` ...) are left alone: nobody meets them in a drop, and a leak costs nothing.

calves.reason: Same as `thieves`: `calve` is a real verb, `calf`/`calves` is the pair.

crises.reason: The "-es" -> "-is" plural, shadowed by `cris` (a dagger; the sibilant stem reads as the two-letter strip and lands on it).

dolmen.reason: A dolmen is a megalithic tomb; a dolman is a hussar's jacket. The "-men" -> "-man" plural rule reads one as the plural of the other, which would refuse a legitimate second answer.

during.reason: The preposition, not a tense of the archaic `dure` (to last) it descends from. The 2026-09-10 spelling rule is what reaches it: `dur` stops being a reading of the ending, so the only one left is `dure`, and a puzzle that had taken the preposition would refuse the verb. Scoring exempts the same word for the same reason -- the two files agreeing here is a coincidence of one shared misreading, not the rule.

germen.reason: A germen is a rudimentary ovary, unrelated to anything German. The "-men" -> "-man" plural rule reads it as a plural of `german`, which would refuse one of the pair; pinned to itself so it keys only onto its own plural `germens`.

halves.reason: Same as `thieves`: `halve` is a real verb, `half`/`halves` is the pair.

indices.reason: The "-ices" -> "-ex" plural, shadowed by the curated `indice`.

limen.reason: A limen is a sensory threshold; a liman is a coastal lagoon. Same "-men" misfire as `dolmen`.

nomen.reason: A Roman clan name, not a plural of `noman`. Same "-men" misfire as `germen`.

selves.reason: `selve` is a curated word and the one-letter strip reaches it first, so the plural of `self` never got to `self`.

shelves.reason: Same as `thieves`: `shelve` is a real verb, `shelf`/`shelves` is the pair.

somen.reason: Somen are wheat noodles; soman is a nerve agent. Same "-men" misfire as `dolmen`.

theses.reason: The plural of `thesis`, but the decisive "-s" strip lands on the unrelated `these` -- so both frequency and spelling pick the wrong root, and only a review can settle it. Pinned to `thesis`, which is also what src/data/score-overrides.json had to do for the score. Note the two files disagree on purpose: scoring caps `theses` at `these` to deny it a Legend, identity must keep them apart.

thieves.reason: Same as `selves`. `thieve` is a real verb, so this picks the pair a player means -- `thief`/`thieves` -- and lets `thieve`/`thieves` through.
